Register a solver backend

Source: R/solver-registry.R
opt_register_solver.Rd

Adds a backend to the registry used by opt_solve() and opt_solvers(), so packages and users can connect other solvers without changing optcompR. Registering an existing name replaces that backend.

Usage

opt_register_solver(
  name,
  solve,
  classes,
  package = character(),
  description = name,
  convex_only = character(),
  global = classes,
  features = list(),
  version = NA_character_,
  priority = 50L
)

opt_unregister_solver(name)

Arguments

name

Backend name used in opt_solve(solver = ).

solve

The solve function described below.

classes

Problem classes the backend accepts (see opt_classify()).

package

R packages the backend needs; the backend is available when all of them are installed. character() for none.

description

One line shown by opt_solvers().

convex_only

Classes accepted only when convexity is proven.

global

Classes the backend solves to global optimality; for other classes it is treated as a local solver (an "optimal" result becomes "locally_optimal" unless the model is proven convex), whatever the local field of its results says.

features

Named list of capabilities: duals, ranging, warm_start, time_limit, mip_gap, iteration_limit (logical), cones (cone types such as "soc", "exp", "pow", "psd") and special ("indicator", "sos": handled natively, otherwise reformulated).

version

A function returning the solver version string, or a string.

priority

Order in automatic selection; lower is tried first. The built-in backends use 10 to 90.

Value

The backend name, invisibly. opt_unregister_solver() returns TRUE when a backend was removed.

The solve function

solve(sf, cls, control) receives the opt_standard_form() sf of the model (parameters substituted; for indicator and SOS constraints that the backend does not list in special, already reformulated with binary columns and rows), the opt_classify() result cls, and control, a list with time_limit (seconds, Inf for none), mip_gap (NULL for the solver default), verbose, warm_start, options (the options list given to opt_solve()) and cache, an environment kept per model and backend in which a backend may store state, such as a basis, for the next solve of the same model. sf$structure_key changes whenever the model structure does. The objective is 0.5 x'Qx + c'x + offset in the sense sf$sense, or, when sf$objective_kind is "nonlinear", the lowered expression sf$objective_lowered, which opt_gradient() and the other derivative functions evaluate. It returns a list with

  • termination: one of the statuses documented in opt_status();

  • primal_status and dual_status: "feasible_point", "infeasible_point", "no_solution", "not_available" or "unknown";

  • x: the column values (length length(sf$c)), NA when there is no point;

  • objective: the objective value including sf$offset, or NA;

  • optionally row_dual and col_dual (shadow prices \(\partial f^* / \partial b\) of the rows and of the column bounds, in the user's sense), gap, bound, iterations (a named numeric vector), message, local (TRUE for local solvers, which turns "optimal" into "locally_optimal"), warm_start, warnings (a character vector), extra (a list) and raw (the solver's own output).

The result is checked: a missing or unknown status, or an x of the wrong length, is an error naming the backend. The returned point is then checked against the model, so a feasibility claim the point does not meet becomes "infeasible_point" (see opt_solve()); an "unknown" primal status whose point passes becomes "feasible_point".

Examples

# a backend that hands LPs to HiGHS through the highs package
my_lp <- function(sf, cls, control) {
  s <- if (sf$sense == "max") -1 else 1
  r <- highs::highs_solve(L = s * sf$c, lower = sf$lower,
                          upper = sf$upper, A = sf$A,
                          lhs = sf$row_lower, rhs = sf$row_upper)
  ok <- r$status == 7L
  list(termination = if (ok) "optimal" else "unknown",
       primal_status = if (ok) "feasible_point" else "no_solution",
       dual_status = "not_available",
       x = if (ok) r$primal_solution else rep(NA_real_, length(sf$c)),
       objective = if (ok) s * r$objective_value + sf$offset else NA_real_)
}
opt_register_solver("my_lp", my_lp, classes = "LP", package = "highs",
                    description = "HiGHS LP through a user backend")
m <- opt_model("max")
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", lower = 0, upper = 3)
opt_objective(m, 2 * x)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m, solver = "my_lp"))
#> [1] 6
opt_unregister_solver("my_lp")
